🟦EVENING NEWS RECAP — March 25, 2026

⭕️BREAKING —

• Bus plunges into Bangladesh’s Padma River; at least 35 passengers missing, search ongoing.

• Footage shows alleged Iranian SAM engagement against a U.S. F/A-18; U.S. confirms no aircraft shot down.

• Iran rejects U.S. 15-point proposal; says war will end only on its terms.

U.S. —

• White House rejects Elon Musk’s offer to fund TSA salaries over legal concerns.

• President Donald Trump announces upcoming meeting with Xi Jinping in Beijing (May 14–15).

• U.S. officials exploring potential Iran talks in Pakistan; timing remains fluid.

• Speaker Mike Johnson says Operation “Epic Fury” may be nearing conclusion.

• Rep. Nancy Mace opposes deploying U.S. ground troops to Iran.

• Trump pushes for FISA Section 702 extension while emphasizing reforms.

Israel —
• Benjamin Netanyahu says campaign against Iran is ongoing.

• IDF continues strikes on Iranian weapons production, missile infrastructure, and air defenses.

• Hezbollah rocket fire injures Israeli reservists in southern Lebanon.
• IDF eliminates armed infiltrator near Gaza ceasefire line.

• Israel expanding northern buffer zone; increased control reported in southern Lebanon.

• Egoz unit captures Hezbollah-linked commander in Mount Dov raid.

IRAN —

• Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi: “No talks with the U.S.”

• Iran reinforces Kharg Island amid concerns of possible U.S. operation.

• IRGC threatens regional infrastructure if Iranian territory is targeted.

• Strikes and air defense activity reported in Mashhad and Tabriz.
• Mojtaba Khamenei reportedly accelerating regime decision-making.

• Iran continues restricting Strait of Hormuz access to select countries.

LEBANON —

• Hezbollah commander captured; Israeli strikes hit operatives and infrastructure.

• Continued Hezbollah rocket fire; Israeli troops injured.

• Hezbollah leadership vows continued fighting “without limits.”

• Expanded Israeli ground activity and buffer zone operations reported.

GULF —

• Kuwait dismantles Hezbollah-linked terror network; multiple arrests made.

• UAE intercepts UAVs; reports extensive missile/drone defense activity.

• Gulf states jointly condemn Iran’s regional attacks and proxies.

• Waterspout reported off Saudi Arabia’s Tabuk coast (non-military).

GLOBAL —

• UN Secretary-General António Guterres calls for de-escalation.

• France coordinating effort to secure Strait of Hormuz maritime routes.

• Japan to deploy ~1,000 troops to Philippines for joint exercises.

• Ukrainian strikes disrupt ~40% of Russian oil export capacity.

• Meta and Google found liable in U.S. court over social media addiction case.

• Bangladesh rescue operations ongoing after deadly river accident.

That's your daily Israel recap. Like, comment, share and repost.

data.text:
NEW - For the first time since 1945, Japanese combat troops are set to deploy to the Philippines for the 2026 Balikatan exercises — a historic shift backed by the Japan-Philippines Reciprocal Access Agreement that entered into force in September 2025.

This is not symbolic. Live-fire drills, command-and-control exercises, and real interoperability — all targeting South China Sea contingencies. Japan and the Philippines are now linking two fronts Beijing previously managed separately, and Japan's post-WWII pacifist constraints are visibly eroding.

Beijing's own aggression has accelerated this alliance integration.

80 years later, Japanese combat boots are back in the Philippines — is this the alliance headache Beijing always feared?

quoted_tweet.text:
@disclosetv This is an interesting ....
Japan is deploying ~1,000 combat troops to the 2026 Balikatan exercises, the first Japanese combat forces on Philippine soil since WWII. Backed by their Reciprocal Access Agreement (signed July 2024, in force September 2025), both nations are building real interoperability through live-fire drills, not just symbolism, targeting South China Sea contingencies. 

For Beijing, this is a headache: Japan and the Philippines are now linking two fronts China previously managed separately, and Japan's post-WWII pacifist constraints are visibly eroding. Beijing's own aggression has accelerated exactly the alliance integration it feared most.

Is this Japan finally stepping out of its post-WWII pacifist shell, or is this still largely a US-choreographed move?
